clue.text: Cigarette butts etc partially reflected in glass vessel

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone spots cigarette ends mirrored in a piece of laboratory glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks EBUTTSET out of cigarettE BUTTS ETc, and 'reflected' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender glass tube closed at one end, used in laboratories, is a glass vessel.

clue.text: Deprived of voice, killed father in retaliation

indicators.note: in phonetics a voiced sound loses its voicing, so the voiced D sounds become unvoiced T sounds

parts.note: did for is slang for killed
dad is father

explanation.surface: A man struck dumb has murdered his father in revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deprived of voice' is phonetics: D is the voiced partner of T, so each D in DID FOR DAD becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a blow given for a blow, repaying an injury in kind as retaliation.

clue.text: New firm favourite at agricultural show?

definitions.meaning: a ..., tup being a ram, would be the favourite at a farming show

explanation.surface: A fresh business venture becomes the darling of a county farm show.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is a ram; the question mark flags reading the word as STAR TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly launched small company, often in technology, is called this.

clue.text: Return of first of services, badly placed, gives one the game

indicators.note: return means come back, so these letters are read backwards
first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a serve badly placed ends up in the net

explanation.surface: A poor serve, badly placed, hands an opponent the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' and 'services' sound like tennis shots, but 'Return of' turns S IN NET round.
explanation.definitionFit: This racket sport, played over a net, is one example of a game.

clue.text: Composer dipping toe into water during drunken revel

indicators.note: the composer's last letter, his toe, dips into the water word

parts.note: J. S. Bach is the composer
a canal is a stretch of water

explanation.surface: A composer paddles his foot in a canal during a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dipping toe into' moves BACH's final H into CANAL, giving BAC then CHANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Named from the rites of Bacchus, god of wine, the word means a wild drunken party.

clue.text: English cartoonist killing off English cartoon character

indicators.note: killing off says a letter is removed from the cartoonist's name

parts.note: H. M. Bateman was an English cartoonist famous for his 'The Man Who...' drawings

explanation.surface: One English cartoonist does away with a cartoon character from England.
explanation.definitionFit: The caped crusader of DC comics is a superhero who appears in cartoons and comic strips.

clue.text: Medal on offer at last for a tanner

indicators.note: on says the medal word is followed by the next piece

parts.note: bronze is the third-place medal

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A medal goes up for sale in the end, for sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin, but here it is a cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic powder or lotion that gives skin a suntanned look is a tanner.

clue.text: Irish curse adopted by the poor

indicators.note: adopted by says the first pieces are taken into the next word

parts.note: drat is a mild curse

explanation.surface: An Irish oath is picked up by the poorest in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the poor' reads as poor people, but 'the' gives letters and 'poor' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality is called this, so it means poor or shoddy.

clue.text: Suspended a Turkish male worker

parts.note: bey was a Turkish title of respect for a man
the ant is the crossword's typical worker

explanation.surface: A Turkish employee has been laid off pending inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in abeyance is held in temporary suspension, not active.

clue.text: Refreshment at regular intervals during the day

indicators.note: at regular intervals says take every other letter of the words that follow, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A drink is served at fixed times throughout the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of the hot drink, or a light afternoon meal, is a common British refreshment.

clue.text: Woman starts to take interest in raw material of DNA

indicators.note: in says the woman and the initials sit inside the word for naked

parts.note: raw can mean naked, as in stripped to the raw
Cleo is a woman's name

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A woman begins to take an interest in the raw stuff of genetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raw material' looks like one phrase, but 'raw' belongs to the wordplay and the definition is 'material of DNA'.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA is a chain of these units, each a base, sugar and phosphate, so they are its building material.

clue.text: Bout or fight not starting straight away

indicators.note: not starting says each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxing bout or a scrap that never gets going at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' beheads Bout, or and fight, leaving OUT, R and IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright as an adverb means at once or immediately, as in being killed outright.

clue.text: Retrograde sequence of approximately one dozen signs

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means approximately
I is the Roman numeral for one
doz is the usual abbreviation for dozen

explanation.surface: An astrologer talks of a planet's retrograde motion through about twelve signs.
explanation.walkthrough: Retrograde is also an astrological term, which suits the surface; here it turns CAIDOZ backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve astrological signs together make up this band of the heavens.

clue.text: They finally opt for rendering which is literal, perhaps

indicators.note: rendering means making into something else, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Translators in the end choose a literal rendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literal' looks like a translation style, but in printing a literal is a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: In publishing a literal is a printing mistake, and a mistyped character is one example.

clue.text: Regulation requiring one to carry guns

indicators.note: to carry says the guns word holds the letter for one inside

parts.note: ordnance means artillery, big guns
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rule requires each person to bear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A local law or authoritative decree is a regulation.

clue.text: Bury footballers find it hard relating to different religions

parts.note: to inter is to bury
FA is the Football Association, the body of English football
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Players of Bury, a northern English football club, find life tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is an English town with a football club, so the capital hides the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialogue between faiths, such as Christian and Muslim groups, is described as interfaith.

clue.text: Shakiest point of long poem with short introduction

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: entree means access or introduction, as in gaining entree to society

explanation.surface: An epic poem gets a brief preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the final E from ENTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above an earthquake's origin shakes the most.

clue.text: Tickle or hug girl, such a classic figure

indicators.note: tickle means stir up playfully, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Tickling or hugging a curvy girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tickle' rearranges OR HUG into HOURG.
explanation.definitionFit: A curvy female shape with a narrow waist is traditionally likened to a sand timer.

clue.text: Brave man has change of heart after painful cut

indicators.note: after says the reshuffled big cat comes behind the painful word

parts.note: a tender spot is sore or painful

indicators.note: change of heart says the middle letters of the brave one swap places

parts.note: a lion is a brave man, as in lionhearted

explanation.surface: A brave fellow relents after a painful wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' swaps the central I and O of LION to give LOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This tender strip of meat from beside the backbone is a prized cut of beef or pork.

clue.text: Scrub out old witticism written on sides of garage

parts.note: ex means former or old
a pun is a play on words, a witticism

indicators.note: sides of takes the outer letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs off an old joke graffitied on a garage wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase or delete something completely is to scrub it out.

clue.text: Marriage guidance counsellors meeting daughter of one family

parts.note: Relate is the British charity offering couples counselling, formerly the Marriage Guidance Council

explanation.surface: Marriage counsellors meet a daughter from a family.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate is a British relationship counselling charity.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are kin, sharing blood or marriage, are said to be of one family.

clue.text: Jacob's brother and son drowned in France?

indicators.note: drowned in says the letter for son goes inside the water

parts.note: eau is French for water, which is what one drowns in, in France

explanation.surface: A biblical brother and his son meet a watery end in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'France' stands for French water, EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the hairy elder twin who sold his birthright was the brother of Jacob.

clue.text: They want wives to become houris periodically

parts.note: to suit is to become, as in that hat becomes you

indicators.note: periodically picks every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Men want wives who turn into beautiful nymphs from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Houris are beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise; 'become' means look good on.
explanation.definitionFit: Men courting women in the hope of marriage are seeking wives.

clue.text: Show increasing interest in picking up a bunch of sailors

indicators.note: picking up, as in picking up a signal, means hearing, so the phrase is said out loud

parts.note: a crew is a ship's company of sailors

explanation.surface: Someone shows growing interest in recruiting a gang of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' is financial: money accumulating interest grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is said to gather interest over time, growing as it builds up.

clue.text: Pains travelling length of backbone

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters change position

explanation.surface: Pains shoot all the way down someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'length of backbone' reads as one phrase, but 'length' gives L and the definition is 'of backbone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to the spine, the backbone.

clue.text: Pretty fine plate

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an etching is a print, or plate, made from an etched metal plate

explanation.surface: A rather nice piece of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty fine' reads as 'quite good', but 'Pretty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching describes something attractive or charming in looks, the same as pretty.

clue.text: Nottinghamshire's opener on course to be complete dud

indicators.note: opener says take the first letter of the county name

parts.note: a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: Nottinghamshire's opening batsman, in cricket, looks set to be a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' and 'course' suggest cricket or racing, but the course is a meal's first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or person with no chance of success is a hopeless failure, a dud.

clue.text: Eggs on valiant army at the front

indicators.note: at the front says take the leading letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A leader urges a brave army forward at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' looks like a verb meaning urges, but 'Eggs' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin plural names female reproductive cells, which are eggs.

clue.text: Lead to guillotine

definitions.meaning: to lead is to be at the head, read as two words
the guillotine cut off heads, so this sense is decapitate

explanation.surface: Someone is taken to the scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead to' reads as escort towards, but 'Lead' is split off as be head.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to be in charge; as one it means to decapitate.

clue.text: Defeats and stops spots, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the word stops read backwards becomes spots, so it turns round

explanation.surface: A team's losses, and the cleaning up of blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Setbacks in battle are called this, and the word also means turns back to front.
